Mashwi Yaed Bayat Al Qubaisi served as deputy managing director of National Investment Corporation in Abu Dhabi. A ruler's decree later appointed him to NIC's board. His responsibilities were executive and fiduciary: NIC, rather than Al Qubaisi personally, developed Marina Mall and the corporation's other breakwater projects.

Separate from NIC, Al Qubaisi commissioned a multistorey Abu Dhabi office building and leased an office to a listed Singapore company. These transactions show a commercial-property interest, although they do not define a dominant wealth-producing enterprise. His present occupation and any family ties to other Al Qubaisi business figures remain private; inheritance, company shareholding and the origin of his wealth are also undetermined.

uncertainties.detail: The immutable and Turkish court records use Mashwi Yased Bayat Al Qubaisi. Abu Dhabi decree, regulatory and property records use Mashwi Yaed Bayat Al Qubaisi, while some building addresses insert a second Mashwi in the patronymic. The distinctive name and shared Emirati-Abu Dhabi context support one identity at 91, but the dossier preserves the variants rather than silently normalising them.

An Abu Dhabi ruler's decree appointed Al Qubaisi to NIC's board, and reporting identified him as deputy managing director. Appointment and management responsibility do not establish ownership of NIC, Marina Mall or the corporation's other developments, all of which remain attributed to NIC.

A contractor identifies him as client for an Abu Dhabi office building, and a regulated offer document identifies him as an office lessor. These records support a personal commercial-property interest but do not disclose title history, beneficial co-owners, portfolio scale or whether property is his principal wealth source.

No reliable source reviewed identifies Al Qubaisi's parents, spouse, children or relationship to other prominent Al Qubaisi figures. Shared surname and patronymic fragments are not used to attribute family companies, state roles or assets.

NIC's current official board does not include Al Qubaisi, and no reliable current biography or operating-company profile was found. His historical executive service therefore cannot support a current primary-industry or operator classification.

All four classifications remain Unknown because no source identifies the original wealth-producing sector, current dominant private business, acquisition route or relationship to a principal asset. The historical NIC role and property evidence are reported without being inflated into wealth conclusions.
